I had a great experience at Loving Touch Grooming Salon. The staff was friendly, professional, and took excellent care of my dog. They listened to exactly what I wanted, and the grooming came out even better than I expected. My dog looked amazing, smelled great, and seemed comfortable and happy when I picked him up. The salon was clean, the service was on time, and the pricing was fair. I’ll definitely be bringing my dog back. Highly recommended!

Unfortunately, the experience at the front desk has become impossible to overlook. The gentleman working as the receptionist is consistently unprofessional, unpleasant, and unnecessarily difficult to interact with. Customer service is just as important as the quality of the grooming, and after today’s experience, I can no longer justify returning.

I’ve been bringing my dog to this salon for about 5 years, and unfortunately the experience has gone downhill since the ownership/management changed in 2025. What used to be a reliable and professional place now feels completely careless and unprofessional.

Over the past 6 months I’ve dealt with mixed-up appointments, an unfriendly attitude from the girl at the front desk, and multiple times getting my dog back with wet hair, knots still in his coat, and even small cuts around his ear. It’s been disappointing to see the decline, but today’s experience was the final straw.

This morning I dropped my dog off at 8:20am for a BATH ONLY. I was told it would take about 3 hours, so I expected him to be ready around 11:20am. At 1pm I called to check in and was told they had fallen behind but he was on the table and they were “blow drying him now” and he’d be ready in about an hour (around 2pm). By 3pm I still hadn’t heard anything, so I decided to just go there because there’s no reason a blow dry should take two hours.

When I arrived, the woman at the front desk had a bad attitude and immediately asked why I was there since no one had called me. She went to “check on him,” but from where I was standing I could clearly see my dog sitting in a cage with his hair still half wet and no one working on him at all.

Not only was I lied to earlier when they said they were working on him, but my dog had been sitting in a cage with wet hair for hours. Anyone who cares about dogs knows that leaving them like that can lead to ear infections and other issues. The best explanation I was given was that the person blow-drying him was “new,” which does not excuse the lack of honesty, the poor communication, or the way my dog was handled.
It’s honestly sad because I supported this business for 5 years, but the service and professionalism have clearly deteriorated.

I won’t be bringing my dog back, and unfortunately, I can’t recommend this place to anyone. If you value honesty, communication, and proper care for your pet, this is no longer the place it used to be.
Love Luis so does Muffin

I strongly advise avoiding this business due to their complete lack of accountability and professionalism when a dog is injured in their care.
I initially brought my dog here for grooming and shortly afterward noticed he would not allow me to touch his ears. I took him to the veterinarian the following day, where the doctor confirmed that both of his ears had been cut as a result of poor grooming. That vet visit cost me $430, directly due to their negligence. Despite this, I chose not to confront the business at the time and continued using their services, hoping this was an isolated incident. I also made it very clear going forward that they needed to be extra cautious with his ears but never shared the fact that I went to the vet even though I have the receipt from the visit.
Unfortunately, one year later, the same thing happened again. My dog’s grooming was not only botched but once again both of his ears were cut in multiple spots. He is now walking lopsided, cries when his ears are touched, and refuses to play- the same symptoms he experienced the first time. He is clearly in pain.
When I informed the business that I would like to speak with the owner, I was met with shocking unprofessionalism and a complete lack of empathy. The owner refused to take accountability, stating, “if I were to take accountability for every vet bill, I would be out of business.” That statement alone speaks volumes.
Instead of addressing the injuries, she made sarcastic and dismissive comments, including suggesting my dog may have gone swimming- which is not possible as we do not have a pool. I personally showed her his visible lacerations on his ears as well as videos of him crying and walking unevenly. She still denied responsibility and offered nothing other than fixing the UNEVEN haircut at no additional charge, as if that somehow resolved the injury to my dog!
I even suggested she speak directly with the veterinarian next door or review a doctor’s note confirming the injuries were caused by their poor grooming. Her response was that the veterinarian “wouldn’t know” whether grooming caused the injuries… effectively questioning a licensed medical professional.
The first time this occurred, I absorbed the financial and emotional cost because I try to avoid conflict. This time, I refuse to stay silent. My dog was under your care and now he is hurt.
The owner stated that she wasn’t the individual who cut my dog and proceeded to put her employee on the spot in front of other clients mind you and said, “I don’t know if you want to eat the cost for this but I will not take the financial hit for something I did not do”
It was only after I stated that I would dispute the charge through American Express and pursue legal action that she finally agreed to refund the grooming. With a foul attitude of course. Demanding I say please. Joke of a lady.
As pet owners, it is our responsibility to protect our animals from harm, and I would be doing my community a disservice if I did not share this experience.
If your dog is mistreated at this establishment, do not expect accountability, compassion, or integrity. Based on my experience, this business prioritizes money over the well-being of the animals in their care.

I had the unfortunate experience of picking up my dog today from a RUDE lady claiming to be the owner. As I go in to pick up my dog the lady starts off by saying the prices will be increasing (already showing her displeasure with her facial expressions). She goes on stating that as a business practice they increase pricing for customers after a year. *This doesn’t bother me because it’s her business and she can do whatever she wants to do with it (and I understand). But then she goes on stating that because of a certain cut they’re going to have to charge me more TODAY for a service that was already done….WITHOUT INFORMING ME. After I tell her respectfully that they need to tell customers these things before doing this service, she goes on stating that they should have charged me this throughout the year and haven’t done it until now and that I am being “UNGRATEFUL” after I ended up paying the price increase. She continues on stating that it’s common for prices to change during the cut… *This is not the first time I go to a Groomer…if they need to charge you more or they offer an extra service- they’ll let you know or call you.

I did receive a call from the Groomers early…but it wasn’t for me lol they had called me mistakenly thinking I was the owner of two other dogs that had flees. Thankfully my dog is on an anti tick and flee medication called Bravecto.

Moral of the story-COMMUNICATE your pricing and practice’s CLEARLY and treat your frequent clientele with RESPECT.
